_palette.ghostty_black: #334843 Gr33N ansi 8, contrast-adjusted by ghostty's port
_palette.diff_green: ansi256(22), #003300 in ghostty's palette, as bright as diff_red
_palette.diff_green_word: ansi256(28), #004c00 in ghostty's palette, as bright as diff_red_word
_palette._diffs: added diff colors, shared with nvim (diff_*) and VS Code: an -ansi base draws diffs in 256 colors, so diffs point at palette slots that ghostty's config sets exactly; dimmed matches dark-ansi, which reuses the same colors
_palette._comments: code comments use ghostty's slot 8, set to dim_green #0b8700 in ghostty's config
_palette._code_text: plain code text (variables, punctuation) uses ghostty's slot 7, set to fg #16b10e in ghostty's config so it matches nvim's variables
_palette.amber: #ffb000 added: no hax0r theme has a warning color
_palette.selection_tint: #1b2c18 added: Gr33N selection @ 12% over bg, used for selections everywhere instead of solid mint
_palette.prompt_band: #073804 added: fg @ 25% over bg, so prompts stand out; dark_green (1.12:1 vs page) was too faint to find them
_palette.bash_band: #2a3529 added: white @ 16% over bg, as strong as prompt_band but tinted toward bashBorder's white, the way built-in themes tint ! commands toward bash mode's color
_palette.faint: #496767 added: Gr33N cursor guide #b3ecff @ 40% over bg (cursor_line is 25%), for subtle; ghostty_black read at 1.36:1 on prompt_band, where the pinned prompt draws, and dim_green would make faint text the same as dim (inactive) text
_palette._hover: userMessageBackgroundHover also colors expanded blocks, so it's dark_green; cursor_line looked bright
_palette._base: dark-ansi: markdown code and syntax colors ignore overrides and read the base by name, so they take ansi slots from ghostty's Gr33N palette
_palette._unchanged: subagent colors, rainbow_* and chromeYellow are pinned to the dark theme's values so agents stay distinguishable
